title: Ideal-adic lifting of geometrically normal formal fibres over a Nagata closed fibre
statement: For a commutative Noetherian ring $R$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], write $N(R)$ for the following condition: for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$, put $B=R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $C=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}B/(\mathfrak pB)^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]; for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset B$ and every finite purely inseparable field extension $k/\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], the ring $k\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}(C\otimes_B\kappa(\mathfrak q))$ is normal [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Thus $N(R)$ expresses geometrically normal formal fibres at all prime localizations, with geometric normality tested on finite purely inseparable extensions. Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $A$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. If $A/I$ is a Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] and satisfies $N(A/I)$, then $A$ satisfies $N(A)$.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 1 (1-4), printed p.8; Appendix A, Definition A.1(1) and the Nagata Z-ring row, printed pp.14–15, quoting Nishimura–Nishimura, Ideal-adic completion of Noetherian rings II, Theorem A.

proof.text: By [lem-per-adic-nagata-lifting], $A$ is Nagata. Suppose $N(A)$ fails. Among ideals $H$ with $N(A/H)$ false choose a maximal one, and put $R=A/H$. Such a maximal member exists by the ascending chain condition: the union of an increasing chain is an ideal, and its finitely many generators lie in one term. The nonzero ring $R$ is Noetherian, is Nagata by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-nagata-nagata], and every nonzero proper quotient of $R$ satisfies $N$. Quotient ideals correspond to ideals containing $H$. The zero ring satisfies $N$ vacuously.

source.place: Theorem 5.1 Step 1 (1-2)–(1-4); agent adaptation of maximal bad quotient reduction to N, using Marot lifting as a separate input.

proof.text: Failure of $N(R)$ gives primes $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ of $R$ and a finite purely inseparable extension $k/\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ for which $k\otimes_R\widehat{R_{\mathfrak p}}$ is not normal. The replacement of the displayed tensor product in the statement by this tensor product is [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change]. By [lem-weil-pbc-formal-fibre-quotient-iso], it equals the corresponding finite field extension of the generic formal fibre of $(R/\mathfrak q)_{\mathfrak p/\mathfrak q}$. If $\mathfrak q\ne0$, maximality in Step 1 makes that ring normal. Hence $\mathfrak q=0$ is prime, so $R$ is a domain, and the failed test is a generic test over $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$.

source.place: Tag 0BIS, lemma-check-P-ring-easy: quotient identification of formal fibres; same generic-fibre reduction as Kurano–Shimomoto (1-3).

proof.text: Put $J=IR$. The ring $R$ is finite as an $A$-module, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian] makes $R$ complete and separated for $J$, since $I^nR=J^n$. Thus $J$ is proper: otherwise the inverse limit is zero, whereas $R$ is a domain. If $J=0$, the map $A\to R$ factors through $A/I$, and $R$ is a finite algebra over $A/I$. Then [lem-per-finite-algebra-normal-formal-fibres] gives $N(R)$, a contradiction. Therefore $J$ is nonzero.

source.place: Tag 00MA, lemma-completion-tensor; finite-algebra permanence from more-algebra.tex Tags 0BIV and 0BIX.

proof.text: Fix any finite purely inseparable extension $L/K$ and let $T$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $L$. The zero-prime clause of [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] and [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] makes $T$ finite over $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal], $T$ is a normal domain with fraction field $L$; by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-nagata-nagata] it is Noetherian and Nagata. Finite-module completeness makes $T$ complete for $JT$, again by equality of the module and ring powers. The ideal $JT$ is nonzero since $R\subseteq T$, and is proper since otherwise separatedness would make the nonzero ring $T$ zero.

source.place: Tags 032R (definition-nagata), 032F (definition-N), 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor); normal finite normalization preparation in the source, (1-3).

proof.text: For a nonzero proper ideal $U\subset T$, choose $0\ne t\in U$. Integrality gives a monic equation for $t$ over $R$ with nonzero constant coefficient: remove any factors of the variable from a monic equation, using $t\ne0$ in the field $L$. Its constant coefficient belongs to $tT\cap R\subset U\cap R$, so $h=U\cap R$ is nonzero and proper. The finite $R$-module generators of $T$ descend to generators of $T/U$ over $R/h$. Step 1 gives $N(R/h)$; [lem-per-finite-algebra-normal-formal-fibres] therefore gives $N(T/U)$. All hypotheses of [lem-per-normal-minimal-quotient-analytic-normality] now hold for $(T,JT)$, so every $\widehat{T_{\mathfrak t}}$ is a normal domain.

source.place: Theorem 5.1 Step 1 (1-3)–(1-4), normal finite normalization and analytic-normality input. Agent reduction from N to this restricted input; no quasi-excellence lifting used.

proof.text: For the prime $\mathfrak p$ of Step 2, [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension] gives $\widehat{R_{\mathfrak p}}\otimes_R T\cong\prod_{\mathfrak t\cap R=\mathfrak p}\widehat{T_{\mathfrak t}}$. Tensor over $T$ with $L$, its fraction field. The product is finite, so tensor distributes over it (component idempotents give inverse componentwise maps). By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], this identifies $L\otimes_R\widehat{R_{\mathfrak p}}$ with a finite product of localizations of the normal domains from Step 5. Each factor is normal by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain]; if the multiplicative set contains zero its localization is the zero ring and is normal vacuously. A prime of a finite product selects exactly one factor, since its component idempotents are orthogonal and sum to one; localization at that prime is the corresponding prime localization of that factor. Thus the product is normal by [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Take $L=k$ from Step 2 to contradict its failed test. Hence $N(A)$ holds.

source.place: Tag 07N9, lemma-completion-finite-extension, and algebra.tex Tag 00GY, lemma-localize-normal-domain; finite-extension cofiber-square argument also displayed in Kurano–Shimomoto Step 2, p.9.

proof_origin.place: Agent maximal-bad-quotient and finite-normalization reduction of the cited Theorem A to its restricted analytic-normality input. Stacks comparison lemmas carry the geometric-fibre assembly. The original Theorem A proof is not available locally; archival source requested in report.md.
